hero: Industrial growth is moderating even as manufacturing expands, while new container support, easier textile incentives and a retrospective allowance increase outline fresh support for production and household income. A tuberculosis patent refusal and a narrower foreign-national bail bar put access in focus; PhonePe is widening its app marketplace into digital goods.

cards.headline: IIP growth eases to 4-month low in September as mining output contracts
cards.brief: Economic Times reports that September industrial output growth eased to 6.7%, a four-month low, with a high base and weaker mining activity weighing on the reading. Manufacturing output grew 7.6% from a year earlier, while electricity generation also increased.
cards.mechanism: The divergence suggests that the aggregate slowdown should be read alongside sector performance when assessing industrial demand.
cards.watch: Watch the next production release for whether mining recovers while manufacturing maintains its expansion.

cards.headline: Cabinet approves ₹10,000 crore scheme to boost container manufacturing
cards.brief: The Cabinet approved a ₹10,000 crore container manufacturing scheme. Business Standard reports that financial support will run until 2039-40, aiming to reduce import dependence, bridge cost gaps and raise annual capacity tenfold to 750,000 TEUs.
cards.mechanism: Bridging manufacturing cost gaps could make domestic container supply more competitive for India's logistics industry.
cards.watch: Watch the support terms and subsequent capacity additions to assess how much of the target becomes usable supply.

cards.headline: Government extends PLI scheme for textiles until 2033-34 to boost MSME participation and investments
cards.brief: The government extended the textiles Production Linked Incentive scheme until 2033-34, Economic Times reports. The ministry reduced the minimum turnover requirement for certain manufacturers from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore, and the reopened application portal will accept submissions from November 1 to December 31.
cards.mechanism: The lower turnover threshold could bring more textile manufacturers within reach of production incentives.
cards.watch: Watch the reopened application window for participation by newly eligible manufacturers and their investment commitments.

cards.headline: Union cabinet approves 3% DA hike for 11.6 million central employees and pensioners, effective July 1
cards.brief: The Union Cabinet approved a 3% dearness allowance increase for employees and pensioners, retrospectively effective from July 1. Economic Times reports that the increase is expected to benefit over 11.6 million people and cost the exchequer ₹10,016 crore.
cards.mechanism: The retrospective allowance increase can lift beneficiary household cash flow while adding to government spending.
cards.watch: Watch the payment schedule to see when the approved increase and retrospective amounts reach beneficiaries.

cards.headline: TB Alliance fails to get patent for six-month treatment regimen
cards.brief: The Indian Patent Office rejected a patent application for BPaL on Tuesday, according to a joint statement by the groups that opposed it, reported by Hindustan Times. The report describes BPaL as a three-medicine combination that has cut drug-resistant tuberculosis treatment to six months.
cards.mechanism: Refusal of this patent application may preserve room for competing supply of the treatment combination.
cards.watch: Watch any challenge to the refusal and subsequent supplier announcements for evidence of changes in treatment availability.

cards.headline: UAPA does not bar bail for all foreigners; illegal entry is key, rules Supreme Court
cards.brief: The Supreme Court ruled that the UAPA bail bar does not apply to all foreigners, Hindustan Times reports. The court said the statutory bar applies only when a foreigner has entered India without authorisation or illegally.
cards.mechanism: Tying this statutory bar to the manner of entry narrows a nationality-based obstacle to bail consideration.
cards.watch: Watch how subsequent bail orders apply the entry condition alongside other applicable requirements.

cards.headline: PhonePe rebrands Indus Appstore, expands into digital goods and webstore
cards.brief: PhonePe is rebranding Indus Appstore and expanding it into digital goods and a webstore, Business Standard reports. The marketplace is present on more than 200 million devices through OEM partnerships and is adding gift cards and top-ups as it seeks wider consumer and developer reach.
cards.mechanism: Adding digital purchases and a webstore could give the marketplace transaction channels beyond app distribution.
cards.watch: Watch whether the expanded offerings convert device presence into repeat consumer transactions and developer participation.

catalysts.text: PM-Kisan: the Prime Minister is scheduled to launch the 24th instalment in Gujarat on October 30, aiming to support over 9.34 crore farmer families nationwide with more than ₹18,680 crore; watch the release confirmation and beneficiary coverage.
catalysts.evidence: On October 30, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to launch the 24th installment of the PM-Kisan scheme in Gujarat, aiming to support over 9.34 crore farmer families across the country with more than Rs 18,680 crore.

catalyst_review: Inspected all captured date-bearing records for October 30. The scheduled PM-Kisan instalment supplies a distinct, quantified national income-transfer deliverable and is not a selected card. The DGFT/Karnataka/FIEO October 30 workshop is awareness training without a separate policy decision. PLI and GST starts and the opposition rally concern November 1; cancer-drug rates begin November 9; trial witnesses, school calendars, the Jharkhand session and the book prize concern later dates. Cyclone warnings and rail disruptions span days without a distinct October 30 action. October 28 earnings and landfall, October 29 trading alerts and the Sudarshan board review do not qualify for tomorrow. No other distinct October 30 catalyst is established.
